title: Sarson ka Saag with Makki di Roti (Punjabi Mustard Greens with Corn Flatbread)
summary: Mustard greens and spinach braised in ghee and water, returned to a garlic, ginger and chilli tadka, boiled briefly and mashed, then topped with salted butter. Served with simple maize-flour roti cooked on a hot pan.
equipment: large sauté pan or Dutch oven with lid

ingredients.item: mustard greens, washed and finely chopped
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Braise the greens
steps.text: Melt 1 tbsp ghee in the pan over medium-high heat, add the mustard greens and 120 ml water and bring to the boil. Cover, lower the heat and cook for 8 min until soft. Add the spinach, cover and cook for 5 min more. Tip into a bowl and wipe out the pan.

steps.title: Make the tadka
steps.text: Heat the 2 tbsp ghee and the oil over medium heat. Fry the dried chillies until they sizzle, then add the garlic, ginger and green chilli for 1 min. Return the greens with the salt, chilli powder and 120 ml water, boil hard for 2 min, then mash firmly off the heat.

steps.title: Make the roti dough
steps.text: Mix the maize flour and salt, then add the hot water gradually and knead for 3-4 min into a soft dough with no cracks. Divide into 4 and press each between baking paper into a 13 cm round about 5 mm thick.

steps.title: Cook and serve
steps.text: Cook each roti on a hot dry tawa for 2 min per side until spotted brown, then brush with a little ghee and press with a spatula until it puffs in places. Spoon the saag into bowls, top with the salted butter and serve with the roti.

tips: Chop the greens finely; it makes mashing much easier.
If the roti dough cracks, wet your hands and knead in a little more hot water.
A spoonful of maize flour stirred into the saag with the last water thickens it in the traditional way.
storage: Refrigerate the saag up to 3 days and reheat until piping hot (74 °C). Make the roti fresh. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
